title: Marco Polo on the Silk Road
description: 1271-1275. Escort the young Marco Polo, his father Niccolo, and their trade caravan across the deserts and mountain passes of Central Asia to the court of Kublai Khan. Bandit raiders and harsh terrain threaten the route; the caravan's pack animals must survive. Victory requires bringing Marco alive to the Khan's summer palace at Shangdu.

anachronisms_found: RICHARD_THE_LIONHEART is placed as the Marco Polo stand-in: Richard died in 1199, some 70 years before the journey, and an English crusader king is the wrong culture and wrong century for a Venetian merchant. Better options existed (a generic Merchant-flavoured unit, a Trade Cart, or a renamed King/heroic unit).
BERSERK x1 in Player Three's 'caravan guards' is a Viking infantry unit with no place on the 13th-century Silk Road; a Militia-line or Camel-line unit would have served.

Player One's escort of KNIGHT x5, CAVALIER x1 and CROSSBOWMAN x5 is a Latin-Christian field army, not a merchant caravan; the Polos travelled with a handful of servants and Mongol safe-conduct, not a Western heavy-cavalry column.
GUARD_TOWER at the Mongol camp is an Imperial-Age fortification more suited to a settled state; Mongol steppe camps of the 1270s were not palisade-and-guard-tower forts.
PIKEMAN x6 guarding the destination (Shangdu) — Yuan garrison troops would be better represented by cavalry archers or spearmen of steppe/Chinese type, not European pikemen.
No TRADE_CART or pack animals are placed anywhere despite the brief insisting 'the caravan's pack animals must survive'; the engine offers trade carts and camels, so this omission is avoidable.

Shangdu, the Khan's summer palace, is represented by a single YURT_A with no palace, wonder, or Chinese/Mongol monumental structure, while the PAVILION_A and MARKET sit with the European player instead.

issues_found: Marco Polo is represented by the RICHARD_THE_LIONHEART hero unit — an entirely different, wrong-century named figure (Third Crusade, 1189-92) who will appear on screen and in the objective panel; the engine allows renaming a generic unit (or using a less anachronistic hero) so this is avoidable.
Niccolo Polo has no distinct representation beyond a lone CAVALIER; the 'Companion Falls' trigger fires on a generic knight rather than an identifiable character.
Kublai Khan is entirely absent — no hero, no named unit, and no palace structure at the destination area (60,30)-(70,50); victory is reaching an empty patch of map.

The caravan itself is missing: the brief states 'the caravan's pack animals must survive', yet there is not a single trade cart, camel, or livestock object owned by Player 1 (the sheep are GAIA), and no trigger references them.

Bandits are built from BERSERK (Viking) and MILITIA plus PIKEMAN — Northern/Western European infantry that misrepresent Central Asian brigands; the engine offers cavalry archers, camel riders, and mangudai as far better fits.

Both active players are set to RANDOM civilization, so architecture and unit rosters are unpredictable rather than plausibly Central Asian/Chinese; the yurts and tents are placed as eye-candy objects, not backed by a civ assignment.

The dialogue 'Ambush! The riders of the Khan were waiting in the rocks!' inverts the history — the Polos travelled under Kublai's protection and carried his golden paiza; the Khan's riders did not ambush them.
CROSSBOWMAN escorts for an Italian merchant party crossing the Taklamakan are a European garrison flavour rather than the small family party the Travels describe.

Marco Polo is represented by the RICHARD_THE_LIONHEART hero — an English crusader king of the 1190s, an unrelated culture and a century too early. The engine ships no Marco Polo, but a renamed Trade Cart, villager or generic cavalier would have been correct and was available.

The brief's central asset, the trade caravan and its pack animals, is entirely absent: no TRADE_CART, no camels, no pack animals of any kind appear in any roster, so the thing the player is supposed to protect does not exist in the scenario.

Niccolo Polo is only referenced in dialogue and a 'Companion Falls' trigger; no distinguishable unit is identifiable as him among the five Knights/Cavalier, so a named principal is effectively generic.
The escort force is five KNIGHTs, a CAVALIER and five CROSSBOWMEN — a Latin-European heavy cavalry company, not a Venetian merchant party travelling under Mongol paiza protection.

The bandit chief is a BERSERK backed by MILITIA — Norse/Western European infantry cast as Central Asian steppe bandits, an avoidable choice when Mongol/Tatar-appropriate cavalry archers, Tarkans or camel riders exist.
Both active players are set to RANDOM civilization, so architecture, unit skins and tech are unassigned for a Venetian caravan and a Mongol/Central Asian opposition.
No structure represents Shangdu (Xanadu): the victory area (60,30)-(70,50) contains no palace, castle, wonder or town centre — the destination the whole scenario is named for is empty ground.

The narrative invents hostility from the Khan's own men ('Ambush! The riders of the Khan were waiting in the rocks!', 'A Mongol camp guards the mountain pass ahead!'). Historically the Polos travelled with Kublai's golden tablet and were escorted and welcomed, not pursued and ambushed by Mongol riders.
The three-and-a-half-year journey via Acre, Hormuz, the Pamirs and the Gobi is compressed into a single generic desert/palm-forest map with no distinguishable stages beyond text triggers.
